column2: On the authority of Abū Yaʿlā Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

“Allah has prescribed excellence (iḥsān) in everything. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare suffering to the animal he slaughters.” Reported by Muslim.

Kataba (“has prescribed”): has made obligatory. ʿAlā kulli shayʾ (“in everything”): ʿalā here has the sense of ilā (“towards”), or keeps its usual meaning. “Prescribed excellence”: in having charge over everything. “So when you kill”:

when you intend to kill, rightfully; “kill well”: in a way that takes the life easily. “And when you slaughter”: when you intend to slaughter, slaughter with a sharp instrument while being gentle with the animal. Dhabīḥatahu (“the animal he slaughters”): the slaughtered animal, in the sense of a passive participle.
The printed gloss reads بما يسح, evidently for بما يسهل (“in a way that makes it easy”).
This hadith is one of the principles of the religion, since excellence extends to everything.
The command to excellence in everything, according to what suits it.
Preparing a sharp instrument when intending to slaughter an animal, and being gentle with it when slaughtering.
The prohibition of torturing and mutilating, whether the one killed or the slaughtered animal.

This hadith contains a beneficial principle: excellence in everything over which a person has control, whether human or animal. Allah the Exalted has made excellence obligatory on him wherever He gives him power over any creature. Then the Messenger ﷺ gave two examples, one for the children of Ādam

and one for animals, so that we may take from these two examples a lamp to light our way in everything that requires gentleness, kindness and excellence. He said: “When you kill, kill well”, that is, by choosing what is lightest

and quickest in taking life, so that the one killed is spared suffering; “and when you slaughter, slaughter well”, by slaughtering with a sharp instrument while being gentle with the animal, so that the slaughtered animal is spared suffering, without torment. “And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good” [al-Baqarah 2:195].
Do good, for a man must surely die, / and you will be repaid for what you strove for.
